_note: SYNTHETIC fixtures — illustrative refusal records, NOT real participant data and NOT claims about any real actor. They exist only to exercise the fold. Reasons are written as a participant might state them; the fold treats every reason as testimony, never as established fact.

_schema.mechanism: which adoption-and-defection.md §4 candidate (4.1..4.6) the participant says would have changed the decision; 'none' is valid and important
_schema.waits_on: (WAIT only) what the participant is waiting on, in their words
_schema.waits_on_actor: (WAIT only, optional) the actor type waited on, when it is a specific side rather than the network at large

refusals.reason: No consumer demand yet. Lowering my integration cost changes nothing while there are no buyers; I will expose structured offers when there is someone to receive them.
The platform already gives me support, refunds, and fraud handling. ARC asks me to give those up for an unproven channel that provides no demand of its own.
I would reconsider only if my earned reputation actually moved with me across communities instead of resetting.
The audit log and approval seam are genuinely useful. The community governance is overhead I do not want, so I will lift the parts I need and drop the rest.
I will build against ARC when there is a network to build for. Right now it is speculative work against users who may never arrive.
We would adopt the open spec and interoperate to gain users, then withdraw federation once the base is ours. The open phase is an on-ramp, not a commitment.
We will run the event types as a compliance veneer and skip the human-approval and disclosure discipline. We want the surface, not the constraint.
Governance is unpaid adversarial labor: fraud reports, appeals, conflict-of-interest checks. Making rulings transparent does not make the work paid.
A centralized app already gives me refunds, chargebacks, and support. A portable audit overlay I could actually act on might change that, but as offered it does not.
Nothing you could add changes that I trust my bank's chargeback more than a community log.
With no merchants, an ARC agent has nothing to do. I will wait until there is somewhere to use it.
The audit and portability benefits accrue to the whole ecosystem; the integration cost lands on whoever moves first. A cheaper integration would remove our first-mover penalty.
